Front: What are the four kinds of method reference?
Back: Static: `Integer::parseInt` (s -> Integer.parseInt(s)). Bound instance: `paymentFunctions::isValidAmount` (p -> paymentFunctions.isValidAmount(p)). Unbound instance: `Payment::getAmount` (p -> p.getAmount()). Constructor: `Payment::new` ((amount, method) -> new Payment(amount, method)). A reference only compiles if the method's shape matches the target functional interface.

`f.andThen(g)` runs f first, then g. `f.compose(g)` runs g first, then f. So `extractAmount.andThen(formatAmount)` and `formatAmount.compose(extractAmount)` both mean Payment → BigDecimal → String. Composing only builds a new Function; nothing runs until `apply()`.

Front: How did Day 20 compose PaymentService methods, and when is composition worth it?
Back: `findPaymentById` (Long → Payment) and `process` (Payment → PaymentStatus) fit together, so `processById` uses `findPayment.andThen(processPayment)` to get Function<Long, PaymentStatus>. The Day 19 not-found exception still applies. Use composition when it improves reuse or clarity; a direct call like `payment.getAmount()` is often clearer than `extractAmount.apply(payment)`.
